Hotlist The contractor will compile a Trouble Ticket Hotlist up to three times per five-day work week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, at the discretion of the 21 CS/CC. These Hotlists shall be sent to all 21 CS Flight Leads and Senior Leadership. This notification email will include all pertinent data on all currently open High Priority tickets and information on any other applicable high visibility projects or concerns. Hands on training from CFP technicians concerning the exact process used to present the relevant Hotlist data will be provided from current CFP government employees during the 90-day military-to- contractor turnover period. The USSF currently operates and supports satellite operation centers at Peterson Space Force Base (PSFB), Schriever Space Force Base (SSFB), Colorado, remote tracking stations and other command and control facilities around the world. USSF personnel monitor satellites during launch, put satellites in their proper orbits following launch, and operate the satellites while they are in orbit, ensuring effective and efficient satellite operations and proper disposal of the satellites at the end of life. award_criteria.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_On_Off_Ramping_Procedures.docx ===== ON AND OFF RAMP PROCEDURES On-Ramping: The Government reserves the right to expand the competitive pool for small business competition at any time during the term of the contract. The Government will advertise the re-opening of the competition on SAM.gov. The evaluation and selection of awardees for any on-ramp will be exactly the same as the evaluation and award criteria used for the MACC initial basic contract awards. Any additions due to on-ramps will not impact the MACC ceiling. The Government anticipates the following awards: Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Awards – The Government intends to make eight (8) awards to the firms comprising the HTROs. The Government anticipates maintaining similar numbers of contracts awarded under each scope throughout the duration of the period of performance but may choose to have more or fewer contracts depending on the availability of qualified offerors and the needs of the Government. Successful on-ramp awardees will compete with any existing or remaining contractors

The USSF currently operates and supports satellite operation centers at Peterson Space Force Base (PSFB), Schriever Space Force Base (SSFB), Colorado, remote tracking stations and other command and control facilities around the world. USSF personnel monitor satellites during launch, put satellites in their proper orbits following launch, and operate the satellites while they are in orbit, ensuring effective and efficient satellite operations and proper disposal of the satellites at the end of life. sla_onsite.text: ===== FILE: files/ATTACHMENT_1_-_AOS_Active_Capability_Gap_28ACG_29_Procedures_26_March_2026.pdf ===== Attachment 1 Army Open Solicitation (AOS) Active Capability Gap (ACG) Procedures Revised – 26 March 2026 SECTION A - ACG SOLICITATION PROCEDURES The below sections outline the competitive procedures to submit an Active Capability Gap (ACG) response to an Army Example Area. These procedures do not apply to Calls for Solutions, which are governed by their own process. This document governs the procedures for all CSO or BAA ACG submissions. ACG Solution Brief submissions will be accepted during the period of availability noted on Army Open Solicitation W9128Z- 25-S-A002) cover page. Any awards resulting from these procedures are as follows: CSO - Fixed price and Fixed Price Incentive awards either using FAR Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Items or Other Transaction (OT) authorities. BAA – Cost type, Fixed price, and other contract types using FAR-based awards and OT authorities. If the Government does not respond to a Company’s ACG submission, then the Government may retain the Company’s submission for consideration at a future date. SECTION B – ACG PHASES OVERVIEW The ACG solicitation portion may consist of up to three (3) phases: Solution Brief

nsideration may be invited to provide a live pitch. The government reserves the right to limit the number of Companies invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be selected for further consideration, however not invited to pitch. The Government will not pay Companies for costs associated with live pitches, unless otherwise stipulated. The Government reserves the right to record live pitches. The Government also reserves the right to bypass Phase 2 in its entirety. Phase 3 – Solution Proposal Companies who are selected for further consideration may be invited to submit a full solution proposal. All awards are subject to the availability of funding. The Government will not pay Companies for costs associated with the Solution Proposal (e.g., proposal development, negotiations) in Phase 3, unless otherwise stipulated. B.1 Guidelines for Solution Briefs, Live Pitches, And Solution Proposals a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. b. When applicable, use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. c. Companies may submit multiple Solution Briefs in response to AEAs, if each submission represents a separate and distinct concept. Individual Solution Briefs may only address one (1) concept i

chedule: The Government will evaluate the feasibility of the Company’s proposed solution/concept project schedule and maturity path. c. Viability: The Government will evaluate the submitted company overview, and if applicable, summary of product/solution commercialization and market strategy for viability. C.4 Phase 1 - Solution Brief Selection Process Based on the evaluation, the Solution Brief will be categorized as Selected for Further Consideration; Retained for Future Consideration; or Not Selected for Further Consideration. Selection into the next Phase will be based on the criteria listed above, Government need, and funding availability. Selected for Further Consideration: The submitted Solution Brief has been determined to be of technical merit, represents a feasible schedule, and the Company is considered viable. Retained For Future Consideration: The submitted Solution Brief has been determined to be of technical merit, represents a feasible schedule, and the Company is considered viable; however, there is no current Government need, manpower and/or funding available. The solution will be retained in a solution repository for future consideration. Not Selected for Further Consideration: The submitted Solution Brief does not represent the necessary degree

sideration: The submitted Solution Brief has been determined to be of technical merit, represents a feasible schedule, and the Company is considered viable; however, there is no current Government need, manpower and/or funding available. The solution will be retained in a solution repository for future consideration. Not Selected for Further Consideration: The submitted Solution Brief does not represent the necessary degree of technical merit, a feasible schedule, and/or Company viability to warrant further consideration. Companies selected for further consideration may be invited to participate in the next Phase, subject to the availability of funds.
